excerpt: Zinier makes no-code field service management software for telecom, utilities, EV charging and other asset-heavy industries. Products, funding and alternatives.
content:
Zinier is a San Francisco software company that sells a field service management platform: the system a business uses to schedule technicians, send them to jobs, track parts and assets, and collect the results from the field on a phone. Its website describes the product as customizable and workflow-based, so an operator can build the processes it needs without writing code. The site's copyright line runs from 2014, and TechCrunch described it as a five-year-old startup in January 2020.

The current product is split into a Z Productivity Suite (scheduling and dispatch, capacity management, parts and inventory, asset and tool management, mobile task execution, forms, timesheets, a customer portal and reporting), Studio Z, a set of no-code and low-code builders, and Z Sidekick, a generative AI assistant. Zinier sells it in Essentials, Accelerator and Enterprise packages and lists integrations with SAP, Oracle, Microsoft, Salesforce, Zendesk, ServiceNow and IBM. The industries it targets are fibre-to-the-premises telecom, EV charging infrastructure, utilities, manufacturing assets and IT equipment. Customers shown on its site include Black & Veatch, NCR, Toshiba, Nokia, Midco and Community Fibre.

On funding, NGP Capital said in March 2019 that Zinier had closed a $22 million Series B led by returning investor Accel, with Founders Fund, NGP Capital, Qualcomm Ventures and Newfund. In January 2020 TechCrunch reported a $90 million Series C led by ICONIQ Capital with Tiger Global, which took its total raised to about $120 million; TechCrunch also reported, citing an investor, a valuation above $500 million, which the company did not confirm. We found no later funding announcement.

Zinier does not publish prices. You ask for a quote, and the package and number of users decide the cost. It suits mid-size and large field operations more than a small contractor with a handful of vans.

This profile is put together from the company's own pages and published reporting, checked on 15 October 2026. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.

profile.summary_short: No-code field service management platform for scheduling, dispatch and mobile work

gallery.alt: Zinier's scheduling console: a dispatcher's timeline of technicians and jobs on a desktop, beside a phone showing a technician's task list
Zinier's logo mark: eight black dots in a circle, two of them joined

use_cases: Scheduling and dispatching field technicians against SLAs
Rolling out and maintaining fibre broadband networks
Tracking parts, tools and assets used on jobs
Building custom field workflows and forms without code

fit: run a field workforce of dozens to thousands of technicians
need workflows that differ from an off-the-shelf tool
already use SAP, Oracle, Salesforce or ServiceNow and want field data flowing into them
not_fit: are a small contractor who wants a cheap self-serve app with published prices

pricing.intro: Zinier does not publish prices. Its site offers three packages (Essentials, Accelerator and Enterprise) and asks you to request a demo for a quote.

plans.name: Essentials / Accelerator / Enterprise
plans.detail: Packages listed on zinier.com; no prices shown

pros: Industry focus on telecom, utilities and EV charging
Integrations with major ERP and CRM systems
cons: Built for larger operations rather than small teams

alternatives.intro: Other products that do a similar job. We have not compared them hands-on; check each one's own site for current prices.

items.name: ServiceMax
items.what: Field service management software for equipment-heavy industries
items.difference: Long-established rival focused on asset-centric service; owned by PTC.

items.name: Salesforce Field Service
items.difference: Best fit if you already run Salesforce for customer service.

items.name: IFS Field Service Management
items.what: Field service part of the IFS enterprise suite
items.difference: Part of a wider ERP and asset-management suite.

faq.a: It sells field service management software for scheduling, dispatch, asset tracking and mobile work, with no-code tools for building custom workflows.

faq.q: How much funding has Zinier raised?
faq.a: TechCrunch reported about $120 million in total after its $90 million Series C in January 2020.
